title: Origins and growth of Hinduism
summary: Hinduism has no founder and no single date of origin. World History Encyclopedia calls it the oldest religion in the world and places its roots in Central Asia and the Indus Valley. Its Vedic period runs from about 1500 to 500 BCE. Its scriptures, the Vedas, include the Upanishads, and their teachings were passed on orally long before they were written down.

uncertainty.note: Hinduism developed without a single historical founder or fixed starting date; the traditional formative era corresponds to the Vedic period (c. 1500–500 BCE).

as_recorded.value: Vedic Period c. 1500 to c. 500 BCE

where.modern_name: Punjab region, South Asia (representative geographic cradle of the Vedic hymns)
where.historical_name: Sapta Sindhu (land of the seven rivers), northern Indian subcontinent

importance.justification: One of the world's oldest living religious traditions, central to South Asian culture.

reviewer_note: Held for review: no institutional source has been opened yet. World History Encyclopedia and Encyclopedia.com are the only sources, and the Pluralism Project pages tried were blocked. The date range is a convention for a tradition with no founder, and the origins remain debated.
